test: the regenerated dynamic state reproduces the frozen passthrough lambdas bit-for-bit
detail: 1900 matches; the passthrough's G1 already anchored those lambdas to Phase 2's stored test-row values, so this chains D2's state to Phase 2 through an artefact that is already frozen

test: no applicable rung/fold selects a lambda on a grid boundary
detail: Amendment 3: G6 is applicable wherever EPV < 10. Applicable at every fitted (rung, fold) here - the highest EPV reached is 3.98

test: with an all-False mask the local pipeline reproduces I4.fit_pipeline bit-for-bit
detail: the pass-through rule of section 6 is the ONLY difference between them; anchoring it here is what makes the new code path readable as Phase 3's, plus one declared change

test: design columns passing through unstandardised
detail: section 6: boolean and indicator columns are neither centred nor scaled. Classified by column KIND, never by observed values

test: DC state is invariant to corrupting every match from the cutoff onward, at 6 probe dates
detail: the window is matches with date STRICTLY < cutoff, so nothing at or after the cutoff can reach the fit. Tested by corruption rather than by re-reading the filter

test: every Elo before-rating follows from earlier matches alone, under Phase 2's declared season-transition policy
detail: 3800 before-ratings checked against continuing / promoted / returning-after-absence, the three cases of Phase 1's transition table. A before-rating that is a pure function of the team's own earlier matches cannot carry information from later ones

test: each match's DC fitting window is exactly the count of matches strictly earlier in date
detail: an off-by-one here would put same-day matches into their own fitting window, which is the classic form of this leak

test: no outer-test row appears in any outer or inner training set
detail: checked across every rung, every outer fold and every inner fold

test: the fitted scaler reproduces exactly from the training rows alone
detail: recomputed independently of the pipeline, from the training rows only; a test row leaking into the scaler would move this

test: design widths match Amendment 3's table A3.2
detail: D3 and D4 are NOT fitted in this session; their widths are computed from the frozen feature file, which is what DS3's nesting claim needs and is not a fit

test: strict nesting D1 < D2 < D3 < D4
detail: the ladder is nested by construction - each rung is the previous column set plus its own

test: D2's columns are D1's columns plus exactly the four dynamic-state columns
detail: checked on the built matrices, not on the feature lists

test: corrupting 2025-2026's features moves no selected lambda
detail: D2, all four folds re-selected on the corrupted matrix

test: corrupting 2025-2026's features moves no OTHER fold's predictions
detail: 2025-2026 is the only season that is a test season and never a training season, so this assertion is not true by construction

test: CONTROL: its own fold's predictions DO move
detail: without this the two checks above would pass on a corruption that never landed

test: corrupting 2025-2026's labels moves no selected lambda
detail: labels of an outer-test season enter scoring and nothing else; if they reached the inner CV this would move

test: D0 reproduces Phase 2's frozen base rate on all six metrics and all three class rates
detail: all four folds; D0 is Phase 2's baseline re-derived, so any divergence would mean the fold structure had moved under it

test: Block C / Block X columns are read from the frozen artefacts
observed: NOT EXERCISED (no C or X column enters D0, D1 or D2)
detail: the frozen feature file's block counts are {'C_context': 12, 'X_prior_composite': 24, 'X_availability': 3, 'X_metadata': 4}; DS10 verifies the file's hash. This test becomes live at D3, which is not run in this session

test: a second full run of every fitted rung reproduces every probability bit-for-bit
detail: Newton from a zero start on a strictly convex objective, and a seeded bootstrap; nothing here should have a source of variation

test: and selects the same lambda at every fold
detail: the selection is a deterministic minimum with a declared tie-break

test: every rung's pooled and per-fold output passes the harness's validate_probabilities
detail: 15 probability arrays checked. The harness raises rather than repairing, so a renormalised break cannot pass silently

test: frozen_manifest.py --verify: no frozen artefact moved hash
detail: PASS - every frozen artefact matches the manifest.

test: extracted DC state through Phase 2's own outcome_probabilities() reproduces dc_walkforward
detail: 1520 test rows; extracted 0.9903635065 against Phase 2's four-fold mean 0.9903635065. The state D2 is built from is the state DC scored

test: every inner split has max(train date) STRICTLY < min(validation date)
detail: 32 inner splits across every fitted rung and fold; the tightest gap is 1 day(s). This is the constraint that forced the calendar date to replace the (season, matchweek) block
